children: Manufacturing activity in the Philadelphia area expanded again in September, albeit at a slower pace than the prior month, according to a survey from the Philly Fed.

In the reserve bank's manufacturing business outlook survey, the current-activity index fell to 37.8 in September from 47.4 in August. A reading above zero indicates an increase in business activity. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal were expecting a reading of 34.
The new orders index ticked down slightly while the shipments index was unchanged the report said.
The employment index dropped 16 points to 11.8, largely undoing a big jump last month when it reached its highest reading since April 2022, but still suggested an overall increase in employment.

Price increases moved higher this month after last month's decline, the survey said. The prices paid index rose eight points to 48.6 in September after falling 13 points last month. The current prices received index jumped 14 points to 31.3, its highest reading since April.
The survey covers businesses in the Philly Fed's district, which includes Delaware and parts of eastern Pennsylvania and southern New Jersey.
